title: The Taylor Swift bridge that explains your week
dek: No fandom exam, no album ranking. Twelve questions about how the last few months actually went, and the bridge that matches the feeling.

questions.prompt: Track one of your month opens with:
The photo you took and didn't post:

options.label: The one where you look happy and weren't
The one somebody else took of you
The group shot you left early in

questions.prompt: You hear their name and your body does:

options.label: A full archive, in order, with dates

questions.prompt: The most you've ever actually said out loud:

options.label: A joke about how badly I'm handling it
Half a sentence, then I left
The kindest possible version of goodbye
Things you almost said, written down

questions.prompt: A friend asks how you're doing. The honest answer:

options.label: Better than I look, worse than I say
I'd do it again and I know better
Waiting for them to go first

questions.prompt: The last time you cried, it was:

options.label: A song, in a car, at a normal volume
A text that was three words long
Something small and stupid and perfect
Rewrite it as a story with a better ending
It was real, we were just late
A lesson wearing a person's face

questions.prompt: I rehearse conversations before they happen.
I still visit the version of it where I said something.

results.name: All Too Well
results.blurb: You remember it in order, with weather. Nothing about it has blurred, which is either a gift or a filing system that needs closing. You're not stuck on the person so much as the detail nobody else noticed.
results.watchOut: The archive is not the relationship. You can stop re-reading the file.

results.name: Cruel Summer
results.blurb: It's not officially anything, which is somehow more intense than if it were. You're doing the most and saying the least, and every small signal gets a full analysis. This is fun. This is also exhausting. Both are true.
results.watchOut: If it has to stay secret to stay exciting, that's information.

results.name: exile
results.blurb: Nobody did anything dramatic. There was just a thing neither of you said, and then a week of not saying it, and now it's a wall with furniture in front of it. You're both waiting for the other one to be braver first.
strengths: Feels the weight of small omissions
Loyal past the point of comfort
results.watchOut: Silence isn't neutral. Someone has to say the plain sentence.

results.name: Anti-Hero
results.blurb: You can name the pattern, the origin and the exact moment you'll repeat it, and you're still going to do it around 11pm on a Tuesday. The self-awareness is real. So is the thing you're being self-aware about.
strengths: Makes the joke before anyone else can
results.watchOut: Naming the flaw isn't fixing it. One small action beats a great monologue.

results.name: august
results.blurb: It was never going to be a whole thing and you knew that at the time. That hasn't stopped it from becoming the reference point for everything since. You're not mourning a relationship. You're mourning a season that felt like one.
strengths: Lets good things be good while they last
Remembers the light, not just the loss
results.watchOut: You keep comparing present people to a memory. Memories don't have bad mornings.

results.name: Delicate
results.tagline: Scared of breaking a good thing
results.blurb: There's something new and it's going well and that's the problem. You're measuring every message, rereading every reply, trying not to be the reason it ends. The care is lovely. The surveillance is not.
results.watchOut: You can't manage a relationship into safety. Ask the direct question.

results.name: The Archer
results.tagline: Ten steps ahead of the conversation
results.blurb: You've already had this argument twice in your head with three different endings. By the time it happens you're bored of it, which reads as cold. It isn't. You just got there first and then hid the map.
results.watchOut: Not everything is a puzzle to solve before it happens. Let one thing be live.

results.name: champagne problems
results.tagline: You ended it and you're still sad
results.blurb: You were the one who said no, and you'd say no again, and it still sits in your chest at odd hours. Everyone thinks you're fine because you did the decisive thing. Decisive isn't the same as painless.
strengths: Knows what you can't live with
results.watchOut: You're allowed to be sad about a choice you'd make again. Don't let it harden into 'I ruin things'.
